title: Prefill credit scheduler and zipper-merge policy for small-span KV reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Small-span queries (common in chat UX with many short turns and retrieval-heavy prompts) cause disproportionate KV slot churn: frequent prefill requests populate many small fragments, then get evicted before reuse, increasing decode latency and GPU memory write amplification. Goal: introduce a credit-based prefill scheduler to prioritize and pace prefill work, plus a zipper-merge policy that opportunistically merges adjacent small fragments into contiguous residency windows to improve reuse and reduce fragmentation. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a canary rollout for dedicated and hosted modes.
implementation_notes: Add per-tenant 'prefill credit' budget tracked in shard admission controller; credits accumulate with idle time and are consumed by prefill requests.
Implement three prefill priority classes: background (low credit), interactive (high credit), and maintenance (forced compaction/merge).

Extend shard allocator with a 'zipper-merge' routine: when two small resident fragments become adjacent in virtual address space and combined size < threshold, mark for coalesced retention and update KV index atomically.
Integrate kernel-selection hints: prefer compact-fusion kernels when zipper-merge is active to avoid decode stalls during coalesced fragments.
Add admission backpressure: if downstream decode queue length > threshold, demote interactive prefill to background pacing to protect tail latency.
Expose telemetry: prefill_credit_balance, zipper_merges/sec, post-merge reuse_ratio, prefill_latency_by_priority.
Implement config flags gated behind runtime-1.19 feature flag for gradual rollout.
decisions: Use soft credits (float budget) rather than hard token counts to allow fractional prefill ops and smoother pacing.
Zipper-merge is conservative: only merge fragments with identical kv-epoch and access-policy to avoid cross-version contamination.
Kernel hinting will be a guidance token in allocator metadata rather than a hard binding to preserve fallback behavior.
No tenant-level hard limits for prefill in this phase; rely on credit starvation + backpressure rather than immediate rejects to preserve UX.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Aisha Patel: Worked through queue/credit model with Daniel; prototype for credit accumulator described in design doc. Linking PRD.
2025-02-18 — Daniel Cho: Implemented local simulator measuring reuse_ratio for synthetic small-span workload. Baseline reuse_ratio 12%; with zipper-merge prototype increased to 41% in sim.
2025-02-25 — María Gonzales (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria; requested explicit canary metrics and cost delta estimation for hosted customers.
2025-02-27 — Daniel Cho: Defensive patch added to ensure zipper-merge only runs when shard free contiguous space >= merged size + slack to avoid creating tiny gaps.
2025-03-02 — Infra (review): Raised concern about atomicity with cross-shard merges; confirmed approach keeps merges intra-shard only.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >= 3x improvement in small-span reuse_ratio vs baseline for targeted workload at p50 latency within 5% of baseline.
No regressions in decode tail latency (p95/p99) on internal CI perf runs for general workloads after enabling feature flag.
Telemetry streaming for prefill_credit_balance and zipper_merges active in staging dashboards with correct labels and units.
Canary rollout plan and rollback path documented; canary customers see cost delta < 8% and tail latency improvement or neutral.
test_plan: Unit tests for credit accumulator (edge cases: credit underflow, double-counting on preempted prefill).
Integration tests: end-to-end prefill flow with demotion/backpressure simulated by variable decode queue lengths.
Bench: run small-span conversational corpus on canary fleet with feature flag on/off and record reuse_ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, and GPU memory churn.
Chaos test: simulate shard eviction while zipper-merge in-flight to validate rollback and consistency.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature flag disabled in prod; run telemetry in staging for 2 weeks (target: 10k requests/day throughput test).
Stage 2: Enable for internal dedicated clusters (non-customer) for 72h; monitor metrics and abort on >5% p99 regressions.
Stage 3: Canary with 3 low-risk customers for 7 days; gather cost/latency metrics and PM sign-off.
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 25% tenant traffic, then to 100% over 2 weeks if stable.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive merging reduces fragmentation but can increase retained memory footprint; zipper-merge threshold must balance these signals.
Compatibility: will not attempt cross-model merges; version pinning enforced by kv-epoch check.
Future: consider tenant-weighted credit accrual policies and ML-based credit burn predictions based on query pattern.
